title: Make K-Subarray Sums Equal
summary: Given a circular array arr and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to make the sum of every subarray of length k equal.
statement: Given a circular array arr and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to make the sum of every subarray of length k equal. An operation consists of incrementing or decrementing any array element by one.
constraints: Treat arr as circular and consider every length-k subarray.
One operation increments or decrements one element by one.
Return the minimum operations needed to make all length-k subarray sums equal.
reference_solution:
def minimum_equal_circular_sums_cost(arr,k):
    import math
    groups=math.gcd(len(arr),k);answer=0
    for start in range(groups):
        values=sorted(arr[start::groups]);median=values[len(values)//2]
        answer+=sum(abs(value-median) for value in values)
    return answer

def minimum_equal_circular_sums_cost(arr,k):
    import math
    groups=math.gcd(len(arr),k);answer=0
    for start in range(groups):
        values=sorted(arr[start::groups]);median=values[0]
        answer+=sum(abs(value-median) for value in values)
    return answer
hints: Equal adjacent length-k sums imply arr[i] must equal arr[(i+k) mod n].
Those index links form gcd(n, k) independent cycles.
All values in one cycle must become equal, and absolute-change cost is minimized by a median.
Sort each cycle, choose its median, and sum distances across all cycles.

tests.explanation: Only indices in the odd-position cycle differ; changing four to three costs one.
All indices belong to one cycle, whose median five gives total cost five.
